quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #21
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: What is the safest way to back up your vehicle?

options.text: Honk your horn right before you shift into reverse.
Walk around the back of your vehicle before you get in the driver's seat.
Look in your rearview mirrors to see what is behind you.
Turn up the car radio before backing up to alert people nearby.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk around the back of your vehicle before you get in the driver's seat.
questions.explanation: Backing up is dangerous because drivers cannot see behind their vehicles easily. Always walk to the back of your vehicle before you get in to check for children and small objects.

questions.question: When should you slow down when exiting a highway?

options.text: On the main road, just before the exit lane.
Once you see a toll booth.
After you move into the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: After you move into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Move into the exit lane well in advance. Start slowing down only after you are in the exit lane.

questions.question: When does your vehicle need more distance to stop?

options.text: On a wet or icy road.
On paved highways.
When driving at night.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a wet or icy road.
questions.explanation: Your car needs more distance to stop on wet or icy roads. Stopping distance also increases on loose gravel or stones.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The highway changes ahead and to the right.
Hiking trails are ahead and to the right.
A hotel is ahead and to the right.
A hospital is ahead and to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: A hospital is ahead and to the right.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that a hospital with emergency services is located to the right.

questions.question: How far before turning must you signal?

options.text: 100 feet
50 feet
200 feet
300 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 100 feet
questions.explanation: You must use your turn signal for at least 100 feet before you turn or change lanes. Signal for a longer distance when driving at high speed.

questions.question: What color are guide signs that show directions and distances?

options.text: Yellow
Red
Green
White

questions.correctAnswerText: Green
questions.explanation: Guide signs have a green background and show directions and distances to places. They are helpful when driving in unfamiliar areas.

questions.question: What is the first step when parallel parking between two cars?

options.text: Turn your wheels to the left.
Turn your wheels to the right.
Pull up next to the car in front of your parking space.
Back up slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull up next to the car in front of your parking space.
questions.explanation: After you find a parking space and check for traffic, signal and stop next to the car in front of your parking space. Then turn your wheels to park.

questions.question: When can you cross two solid yellow lines on a highway?

options.text: Only to turn left into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.
To pass other vehicles if there is no oncoming traffic.
Never.
Only to make a U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only to turn left into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing in either direction. You can only cross them to turn left into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.

questions.question: Why is it important to watch for motorcycles?

options.text: They are harder to see than cars.
They rarely use their headlights.
Motorcycle riders are less skilled drivers than other drivers.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are harder to see than cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are smaller and harder to see than cars. They can hide in your blind spot. It is hard to judge how far away a motorcycle is and how fast it is moving. Always stay alert around motorcyclists.

questions.question: A traffic light turns solid yellow as you approach an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Treat it like a caution sign and continue through the intersection.
Stop right away.
Stop if you can do so safely. If you cannot stop safely, drive carefully through.
Speed up to get through before the red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop if you can do so safely. If you cannot stop safely, drive carefully through.
questions.explanation: When you see a solid yellow light, slow down and stop before entering the intersection if it is safe. If you cannot stop safely, drive carefully through.

questions.question: Traffic signals sometimes show arrows to control turns from specific lanes. What does a solid red arrow mean?

options.text: It is never used as a traffic signal.
It means the same thing as a circular red light.
It means you may turn in the direction the arrow points.
It means traffic in that direction must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same thing as a circular red light.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same thing as a circular red light. You must stop and cannot turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.question: If a green arrow changes to a solid green light, what should you do?

options.text: You may still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
You must stop turning and go straight.
You still have the right to turn without yielding.
You no longer need to turn in the arrow's direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow turns into a solid green light, you may still turn. But you must yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Why does the road become especially slippery during the first half hour of rain?

options.text: Dust and oil on the road have not yet washed away.
Tires have not yet absorbed the water.
Water pools the most at the start of rain.
It rains harder at the beginning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dust and oil on the road have not yet washed away.
questions.explanation: Roads become slippery early in rain because dirt and oil on the surface have not washed away. Water mixes with these materials and creates a slick surface that tires cannot grip well.

questions.question: When turning left onto a one-way street, which lane should you turn into?

options.text: The right lane.
The lane closest to your previous lane.
Either lane.
Neither lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to your previous lane.
questions.explanation: Always turn into the lane closest to where you came from.

questions.question: On a road with no sidewalk, which side should a pedestrian walk on?

options.text: The side with the lightest traffic.
The same side where traffic is moving.
The side facing oncoming traffic.
The side with the heaviest traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: The side facing oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians should walk on the side of the road facing oncoming traffic so they can see cars coming toward them.

questions.question: You see a flashing yellow light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait for the light to change.
Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.
Drive carefully through the intersection.
Get ready to stop; the light is about to turn red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive carefully through the intersection.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and look both ways before entering the intersection.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a stopped school bus with flashing amber lights?

options.text: Stop and stay stopped until the bus passes.
Slow down and be ready to stop.
Honk your horn and pass slowly.
Speed up and pass quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When you see a school bus with flashing amber lights, slow down and prepare to stop. You must come to a complete stop when the bus stops and turns on its red lights.

questions.question: What color are road markings that separate traffic moving in opposite directions?

options.text: Yellow
White
Yellow and white
Yellow, white, and black

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate lanes where traffic moves in opposite directions.

questions.question: What is the first thing you should adjust when you get into a car to drive?

options.text: Your seat belt
The steering wheel
Your rearview mirror
Your seat

questions.correctAnswerText: Your seat
questions.explanation: First adjust your seat so you are comfortable and can see the road clearly. Then adjust your mirrors and steering wheel.

questions.question: You come to an intersection blocked by other traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Go slowly until traffic ahead moves.
Get as close as possible to the car in front.
Stay out of the intersection until you can drive all the way through.
Honk your horn to make cars move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay out of the intersection until you can drive all the way through.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection if you cannot drive all the way through it. Wait until traffic ahead clears.
